Case Study · 02 / 04

The Garden

Designing a more connected women’s health experience: a future vision for care that remembers, guides, and supports women across life stages.

DesignHealthcareResearch

Project Details

Work TypeService design at IDEO
FocusWomen’s health ecosystem vision (Cottage Garden)
My RoleService Designer, Research Partner & Lead Interaction Designer
Timeline8 weeks

The Problem

Women are not being taken care of by the U.S. health system.

Women’s pain is too often ignored or overlooked, and research on women-specific conditions is underfunded and years behind. This is the reality that women face every day when trying to access preventative and life-saving medical care.

A local health system and IDEO tackled this challenge, and asked a big question together:

How might we reimagine the health experience to seamlessly integrate care across touchpoints, systems, and the lived experience of women?

As service designer, research partner, and lead interaction designer, I helped shape a future-state vision grounded in research with patients, caregivers, providers, and staff, from adolescence through pregnancy, postpartum, perimenopause, older adulthood, and breast cancer. From those insights, we developed a new ecosystem of care focused on better navigation, trusted support, and more seamless experiences across the full health journey.

The Process

You can’t design for women’s health by only looking at service lines and clinical workflows. You have to start with women’s actual lives.

29
In-depth interviews with patients, caregivers, providers & staff
10
Diary study entries capturing care experiences between visits
6
Life stages mapped end-to-end across women’s health journeys
3+
Analogous domains explored including doulas & concierge medicine

Our team grounded this work in stories from women across life stages, from adolescence to pregnancy, postpartum, perimenopause, older adulthood, and breast cancer. We spoke with patients, caregivers, providers, and health system staff, and paired interviews with diary work, analogous research, and journey mapping to understand what care feels like not just in the room, but before, between, and after visits.

And while many women described their in-clinic care as warm, thoughtful, and high quality, we kept hearing that the hardest moments happened in the transitions, where systems broke down, referrals disappeared, women had to explain themselves all over again, or support simply stopped once they left the building.

To map that gap, we developed six end-to-end journeys that made visible both the strengths and the seams in the current system: establishing care, pregnancy, postpartum, perimenopause, breast cancer, and older adulthood. These journeys helped us distinguish table-stakes fixes from more transformational opportunities. The biggest needs weren’t tied to one condition; they repeated across life stages: clearer guidance, better handoffs, more continuity, and more holistic support.

The Solution

That gap between excellent care and a fragmented overall experience became the core design opportunity. We translated it into Cottage Garden, a future-state ecosystem, and a set of signature concepts that addressed the patterns we saw in research.

Signature Concepts

True North: helping women see the long view

Women told us they want continuous guidance and foresight across life’s transitions, rather than having insurance dictate which tests and screenings they receive, or discovering life stages only once they’re already in them.

True North is a patient-facing tool that helps women see the long view of their health journey by bringing together their data, priorities, and reflections into a dynamic timeline they can share with their providers. It offers stage-smart guidance with clinically backed themes for each life stage, integrates personal data by linking MyChart and wearable devices, and includes an AI-powered voice diary that weaves women’s reflections into tailored recommendations, highlighting topics to prioritize at their next appointment.

Wellness Commons: a front door to holistic support

Women told us they want access to holistic care and trusted answers to their health questions, instead of turning to social media, Google, or ChatGPT.

Wellness Commons is a curated, personalized library of resources for a woman’s health needs or life stage, vetted by the health system and delivered in a variety of formats including articles, classes, and podcasts. It connects women in Santa Barbara to trusted referrals for acupuncture and other holistic care the health system may not offer in-house. And by leveraging the scale of a health system, it can offer subsidized access to things like meditation apps or strength training memberships, making wellbeing accessible to everyone, not just those who can afford concierge medicine.

Care Circle: right-sized support around the woman

Women told us they want right-sized support for different life stages and phases of their health journey. Investing in 1:1 nurse navigation is critical, but also expensive, and we wanted to make sure support is accessed equitably, by those who need it most, without leaving anyone without an option.

Care Circle assembles an extended support network, connecting women to a care support team and a navigator when needed, delivering tailored support that meets each woman’s specific needs. Anyone who needs help navigating their care has an option that best suits them.

Wrap Up

I love working with and for women. I enjoyed every minute sitting in women’s houses hearing about everything from their church meal train, to their lifelong battle with endometriosis.

At the end of the day women are the glue of a community, so women’s health is community health. I’m excited our client has decided to move forward with this work, and hope they continue to keep women at the center of what they make next!
